main_body: Riveted steel panel floor/wall patch, 4x3 tiles, with a hatch panel and a panel with a cyan light. It is a flat terrain texture, not a standing object.
top_band: none (terrain tile; the column scan only shows repeating panel seams and bevel highlights every 8 rows)
evidence: The kind is terrain, so the standing-object top/front contract does not apply. The piece is a seamless-style tiled surface with no standing volume, no receding side faces and no object silhouette. The repeating seams and bevels are surface detail, so I don't count this as a failed front elevation.

style.evidence: The dark seams are a blue-slate tint (#1c2230) and 0% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is material-toned. Each panel has about 5 steps: a light bevel on top and left, mid-tone fill, a darker inset and deep seams, plus lighter rivet dots. There are no 5x5 flat fills, and the panel patches and rivet dots break up the surface. Median colours per tile is 6, close to the paving reference (7) and well below the grass reference (26). The palette is only 8 colours, which is lean, but it is on par with the paving reference at the same scale and does not read as a sticker.
